title: Correct normal force
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates the normal force as N = mg + F sinθ for both cases.

title: Maximum static friction
description: Important: Student calculates the maximum static friction force f_max = μN for both applied forces.

title: Static equilibrium check
description: Essential: For F=10 N, student correctly determines the object remains at rest because Fcosθ ≤ f_max, resulting in zero net force.

title: Kinetic friction application
description: Important: For F=30 N, student correctly identifies that sliding occurs and uses the maximum static friction (now kinetic) to find the net horizontal force.

title: Final numerical answers
description: Essential: Student provides the correct final answers: 0 N for part (1) and 5 N for part (2).

title: Sign error in friction
description: Pitfall: Student uses the wrong sign for the friction force in the net force equation (e.g., adds it instead of subtracting).

title: Incorrect friction model
description: Pitfall: For F=30 N, student incorrectly uses static friction (f = Fcosθ) instead of kinetic/maximum static friction after determining motion occurs.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Student shows consistent use of units (N, kg, m/s²) throughout the calculation.
